text:
jessica: Escalation from account team — multiple customers reporting sudden cross-region hops after yesterday's routing rollout. They pinned to eu-west-1 but we see traffic to us-west-2 and consumer latency spiked. Getting 403s for some token exchanges. Can ENG/infra please triage?

raj: Noted. Which customers? Any request IDs or sample traces?

jessica: acme-corp and beta-app. Sample trace id: trace_20260301_4872. Logs attached by customer show 401 then 403 on token refresh, then a successful retry from a different region.

kevin: I see similar in our global router logs — looks like failover decisions took effect despite sticky routing enabled for those accounts. Sending snippet: `route_decision(account=acme-corp, policy=weighted, sticky=true) -> chosen=us-west-2 weight_priority=50/50`.

maria: That sounds wrong — sticky should prevent cross-region after session sticky cookie set. Did the rollout change the matching key for sticky?

kevin: Yep. During the rollout we renamed the cookie key from `rw_region_v1` to `rw_region_v2` and left the old fallback; some envs still honor v1, others only v2. If the cookie is missing, policy falls back to weight-based selection.

jessica: Customer says they had active sessions — so cookie must've been present. Could the cookie path or domain mismatch cause it to be ignored? They run behind a CDN.

raj: Good call. CDN might strip/alter cookie domain. Can infra check whether router saw the cookie header on inbound request?

infra-bot: router-logs: show requests where headers.cookie does NOT contain `rw_region_v2` but contains `rw_region_v1`. Example: `GET /v1/generate trace=trace_20260301_4872 headers.cookie=rw_region_v1=eu-west-1;`. Router version=2026.3.2.

maria: Ah — weight-based fallback happens when v2 is absent even if v1 is present. That's a bug in sticky resolution logic introduced to support migration. We'll roll a hotfix to accept either key.

kevin: For immediate mitigation: I can push a config change to prefer legacy key when new key missing (a toggle). Want me to do it?

jessica: Do it. Also need a customer-facing note and rollback plan if this causes regressions.

raj: I'll draft the customer note: short, apologetic, explain root cause (cookie key mismatch during rollout) and mitigation (config toggle + hotfix). Include ask: please clear CDN edge caches for cookie headers?

maria: Hotfix build prepared, will push to staging in 5m and then prod if tests pass. Patch changes sticky resolution: accept `rw_region_v2 || rw_region_v1` and keep previous precedence.

kevin: Toggling prefer-legacy true in prod now (rolling 20% shards to start). Monitoring latency/403s.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: toggle prefer-legacy set true on router-cluster-1 at 2026-03-01T15:40:12Z.

jessica: Customer team notified. They've confirmed initial requests look better but still seeing some 5xxs from us-west-2 — could be in-flight retries.

maria: We'll keep canarying. Postmortem next steps: 1) Add migration compatibility tests for cookie key changes, 2) improve observability to show which cookie key matched for each request, 3) update rollout checklist to include CDN cookie behavior.

raj: Drafted customer note and escalation thread for sales. Sending now.

jessica: Thanks all — keeping this thread pinned to follow updates. :thumbsup:
